requirements_summary.summary: Participium is a web application for the Municipality of Turin enabling citizens to report urban issues (e.g., potholes, trash) via an interactive map or Telegram bot. Reports undergo a lifecycle: Pending Approval -> Assigned (to Technical Office) -> In Progress -> Resolved/Rejected/Suspended. The system supports external maintainers (with or without platform access), internal communication channels, notifications (email/push), and detailed statistics for administrators.

requirements.text:
As an unregistered user
I want to see approved reports on an interactive map 
So that I can know about issues in my area and beyond.
expected_behaviors: I can know about issues in my area and beyond

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member
I want to assign reports to external maintainers
So that specialized maintainers can handle and update the intervention.
constraints: It can be possible for specific reports of certain categories (e.g., Enel X for category Public Lighting) based on their content reviewed by the technical office staff member.
expected_behaviors: specialized maintainers can handle and update the intervention

requirements.text:
As an external maintainer 
I want to update the status of a report assigned to me
So that I can updated citizens about  the intervention.
expected_behaviors: I can updated citizens about  the intervention

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member/external maintainer
I want to exchange information and comments on the report internally
So that coordination happens without exposing internal notes to citizens
expected_behaviors: coordination happens without exposing internal notes to citizens

requirements.text:
As a citizen
I want to register with my name and username 
So that I can access the Participium system and submit reports.
constraints: Registration is required before submitting reports.
expected_behaviors: I can access the Participium system and submit reports

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to confirm my registration with a code
So that my account becomes valid and I can start using the system.
constraints: Once a registration is completed, the user gets an email with a confirmation code. The person can use the application only after confirming by entering the code valid for 30 minutes.
expected_behaviors: my account becomes valid and I can start using the system

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to set up municipality users
constraints: These are the internal accounts of the municipality

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to assign roles to municipality users
constraints: Possible roles: municipal public relations officer, municipal administrator, technical office staff member, external maintainer. You can be more specific on technical offices to run realisti scenarios following the official organizational structure of the municipality of Turin (https://trasparenza.comune.torino.it/media/2212/download)

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to provide details for my report 
So that the the problem is classified correctly.
constraints: Mandatory fields: title, description,  category , photos (min 1 max 3).
expected_behaviors: the the problem is classified correctly

requirements.text:
As a municipal public relations officer
I want to review and approve or reject reports 
So that only valid reports are processed further.
constraints: Rejected reports must include an explanation. If accepted, the report is assigned to the technical office bound to the report category.
expected_behaviors: only valid reports are processed further

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to see approved reports on an interactive map 
So that I can know about issues in my area and beyond.
constraints: Map should be zoomable. When zooming out, reports can be grouped into a cumulative report for a better visualization (total number should be reported on the cumulative report). When zooming in,  reports can be seen separated, with their title and reporter name (or "anonymous" if this is flagged on that report).
expected_behaviors: I can know about issues in my area and beyond

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to choose whether to make my report anonymous 
So that my name is not shown in the public list of reports.
constraints: Anonymous option protects privacy. Choice made at issue description time.
expected_behaviors: my name is not shown in the public list of reports

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member
I want to see the list of reports assigned to me
So that I can get an overview of the maintenance to be done
expected_behaviors: I can get an overview of the maintenance to be done

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to configure my account
So that I can better manage notifications and my virtual presence.
constraints: Citizens can  upload a personal photo, add their Telegram username and switch off/on email notifications in the configuration panel.
expected_behaviors: I can better manage notifications and my virtual presence

requirements.text:
As a citizen/unregistered user 
I want to search for reports in a specific area by typing in an address
So that I can easily explore and analyze existing reports in that specific area.
constraints: You can choose how much to zoom in. The product owner will then provide feedback on the implementation.
expected_behaviors: I can easily explore and analyze existing reports in that specific area

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to modify roles to municipality users
So that the staff can be more flexible.
constraints: This story overwrites a previous answer given by PO on the Telegram chat. NB: 1) A municipality user can now have multiple roles, i.e. serving on more than one technical office. 2) Modification includes cancellation.
expected_behaviors: the staff can be more flexible

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member 
I want to update report statuses 
So that citizens are informed of the problem resolution process.
constraints: At each status change, the citizen receives notification in the platform with the corresponding update. Municipal operators working on reports can also send messages to the citizens in the platform, to which the citizen can reply.
expected_behaviors: citizens are informed of the problem resolution process

requirements.text:
As a citizen
I want to create a new report through a Telegram bot
So that I can quickly notify the public administration about an issue in my area.
constraints:
Allows the citizen to open a new report by selecting a location on the Turin map, entering a title, description, choosing a category, and attaching up to three photos. The bot also asks if the report should be anonymous.

Example command:

/newreport → Starts the guided process to create a new issue report with location, title, description, category, photos, and anonymity preference.
expected_behaviors: I can quickly notify the public administration about an issue in my area

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to access quick assistance and help commands from the Telegram bot 
So that I can understand how to use the system and find useful contacts.
constraints:
Example commands:

/help → Lists available commands and how to use them.

/contact → Provides contact info for the Municipality support team.

/faq → Shows frequently asked questions
expected_behaviors: I can understand how to use the system and find useful contacts

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to reply to messages from municipal operators in the platform 
So that I can communicate directly about my report.
constraints: Two-way communication is possible within the platform.
expected_behaviors: I can communicate directly about my report

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to receive real-time push notifications via the Telegram bot 
So that I know instantly when my report status changes.
constraints:
Example commands:

/subscribe → Enable real-time notifications for all your reports.

/unsubscribe → Disable notifications.

/subscribe report 12345 → Subscribe only to updates for report ID 12345.
expected_behaviors: I know instantly when my report status changes

requirements.text:
As a citizen/unregistered user
I want to browse a summary table of reports with filters 
So that I can easily explore and analyze existing reports.
constraints: Filters: by category, status, period of time
expected_behaviors: I can easily explore and analyze existing reports

domain_rules: Reports must be in 'Pending Approval' state until the Organization Office performs preliminary verification.
Rejected reports require a mandatory explanation from the Municipality Organization Office.
Accepted reports move to 'Assigned' state and are sent to the competent technical office based on category.
Once intervention is scheduled, status changes to 'In Progress'.
When resolved, technical office updates status to 'Resolved' and closes the report.
Internal comments between technical office staff and external maintainers are not visible to citizens or reporters.
Automatic assignment of all issues of a certain category is possible only if previously set by the municipal administrator.
Only authenticated users (citizens) can view reports initially; from Sprint 4, unregistered users can also view reports.
An anonymous user's name is visible to staff but hidden in the public Turin map for citizens.
Once a report has been inserted, it cannot be modified or deleted by the citizen.
Public Relation officer can assign a report either to a specific technical office or directly to a staff member of that office.
Only technical office staff members can have multiple roles.
Notifications/messages can be set to either real-time or on page refresh depending on preference.
External maintainers are added by the system administrator and must have their own individual account (Case 1).
Communication between technical office and external maintainers without platform access is out of scope (Case 2).
Email is a mandatory field for registration and can be used for login.
Confirmation code for registration is valid for exactly 30 minutes.
Reports must be geolocated using OpenStreetMap standard layer.
edge_cases: User attempts to submit a report without registering: System blocks submission until registration and confirmation are complete.
User attempts to view reports before approval: System hides 'Pending Approval' reports from public view.
External maintainer resolves a report: System allows transition to 'Resolved' only if maintainer has access (Case 1).
Citizen tries to edit/delete their own report after submission: System denies action.
User zooms out on map significantly: System groups reports into cumulative view with total count.
User filters table by category and clicks download: System exports only the filtered subset as CSV.
Telegram bot receives command for non-existent report ID: System returns error or 'not found' message.
Citizen follows a report that is later resolved/rejected: System stops sending notifications once status becomes closed.
assumptions: The 'Organization Office' refers to the central administrative body responsible for initial review and rejection explanations.
Competent technical office mapping to categories is pre-configured in the system database.
Telegram bot integration requires a valid Telegram API connection and user authentication via username.
Push notifications rely on Telegram's native push mechanism or an integrated service.
The 'top 1%' and 'top 5%' statistics are calculated based on report volume per reporter over a specific time window (likely all time or configurable).
External maintainers without platform access (Case 2) communicate via external channels not tracked by Participium.
The map layer is strictly OpenStreetMap standard unless overridden by admin configuration.

authentication_notes: Most endpoints require authentication; only /reports/anonymous and /telegram/webhook are public.
User registration requires confirmation via email before accessing authenticated resources.
Operations marked auth_required need an authenticated session during test setup.
dependencies: POST /sessions (login) is a prerequisite for all authenticated operations.
POST /users (registration) must be followed by POST /users/confirm before accessing user-specific endpoints.
POST /reports creates a report ID required for subsequent GET/PUT on /reports/{id} endpoints.
POST /comment/{id}/comments and POST /reports/{id}/messages depend on the existence of the report (created via POST /reports or POST /reports/anonymous).
GET /reports/pending, PUT /reports/{id}/review, GET /reports/assigned require admin or municipal staff roles.
PUT /reports/{id}/status and GET /reports/external/assigned require external maintainer role.
POST /users/admin and POST /users/external-maintainers require admin role.
POST /users/{id}/assign-role and DELETE /users/{id}/remove-role require admin role.
POST /sessions -> GET /reports/me: User must be authenticated to view their own reports.
POST /reports -> GET /reports/{id}: Report ID must exist before retrieving details.
POST /users -> GET /reports/me: User account must be confirmed before accessing authenticated resources.
POST /users/admin -> POST /users/{id}/assign-role: Admin role creation is prerequisite for assigning roles to other users.
POST /users/external-maintainers -> GET /reports/external/assigned: External maintainer must be created and authenticated to access assigned reports.

dependency_edges.reason: User must be authenticated to view their own reports.
Report ID must exist before retrieving details.
User account must be confirmed before accessing authenticated resources.
Admin role creation is prerequisite for assigning roles to other users.
External maintainer must be created and authenticated to access assigned reports.

risks: Ambiguity in role-based access control: some endpoints specify 'admin only' or 'technical office staff' but lack explicit role validation in the schema.
Anonymous report creation bypasses user authentication, potentially leading to data integrity issues if not properly logged.
Telegram webhook endpoint is public and could be exploited for spam or abuse if not rate-limited.
Confirmation code expiration (30 minutes) may lead to failed registrations if users delay confirmation.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Unregistered user wants to see approved reports on an interactive map.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a GET request to /reports/approved. Verify that the response contains a list of reports where status is 'Resolved' or equivalent final states, excluding 'Pending Approval', 'Assigned', or 'In Progress'. Ensure the response format matches the expected map data structure (e.g., GeoJSON features).
setup_needed: Authenticate as a user with the required role.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the core functionality for unregistered users to view public data as per requirement PT28.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: External maintainer wants to update the status of a report assigned to them.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a PUT request to /reports/{id}/status. Set the body to change the status to 'Resolved' and include a resolution comment. Verify that the system accepts this update only if the current user is an authenticated external maintainer assigned to this report.
setup_needed: Create a user with role 'external_maintainer' using POST /users/external-maintainers.
Assign this maintainer to a specific report ID via the assign-external endpoint.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Verify that the report status was updated. If the update failed, ensure no partial state changes occurred. Reset the report status back to its original value if necessary.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the ability of external maintainers to resolve reports as per PT25.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Unregistered user wants to see approved reports on an interactive map.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a GET request to /reports/approved. Verify that the response excludes any reports with status 'Pending Approval', 'Assigned', or 'In Progress'. Ensure that only fully resolved or closed reports are returned.
setup_needed: Authenticate as a user with the required role.
Create a report with status 'Pending Approval'.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete the created report to restore system state.
strategy_items.rationale: Ensures that unregistered users do not see reports that are not yet fully approved or resolved, adhering to domain rules and PT28.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Technical office staff member wants to assign reports to external maintainers.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a PUT request to /reports/{id}/assign-external. Set the body to include an 'external_maintainer_id' that does not exist in the system or is not authenticated. Verify that the system returns an appropriate error (e.g., 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden) indicating that the maintainer cannot be assigned.
setup_needed: Ensure an authenticated session for a user with role 'technical_office_staff_member'.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Verify no resource was created; delete it if unexpectedly present.
strategy_items.rationale: Tests the system's ability to handle invalid external maintainer IDs during assignment as per PT24 and domain rules.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen/unregistered user wants to browse a summary table of reports with filters.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a GET request to /reports/citizen. Include query parameters for filtering by 'category' and 'status'. Verify that the response returns a paginated list of reports matching the filters, excluding internal comments.
setup_needed: Create an authenticated session for a user with role 'citizen'.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the core functionality for citizens to browse and filter reports as per PT22.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen registers with name and username to access the system.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute user registration for a new citizen. Provide a unique username, valid email address, and full name. Verify that the response indicates successful creation or returns 409 Conflict if the username/email already exists.
setup_needed: Authenticate as a user with the required role.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the core entry point for new users as defined in PT01.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen confirms registration with a code to activate account.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute the confirmation flow. Use the token/code received during registration (from PT01) within the 30-minute validity window. Verify that the account status changes to 'active' and the user can now access authenticated resources.
setup_needed: Authenticate as a user with the required role.
Execute POST /users with valid citizen data (username: 'citizen_test', email: 'citizen@test.com') to obtain a registration token.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Ensures the account activation mechanism works correctly after initial registration.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: System administrator sets up municipality users.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute the admin user creation endpoint. Authenticate as a system administrator (role: 'admin'). Create a new municipality user with valid credentials and assign them an initial role (e.g., 'staff' or 'maintainer') to prepare for subsequent role assignment tests.
setup_needed: Ensure the current session is authenticated as a user with 'admin' privileges.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete the created user via DELETE /users/{id} if it was not intended to persist in the test environment.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the admin capability to create users, a prerequisite for role management.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: System administrator assigns roles to municipality users.
strategy_items.prompt: Assign a specific role (e.g., 'technical_office_staff') to the user created in PT02. Verify that the assignment is successful and the user's profile reflects the new role.
setup_needed: Execute POST /users/admin to create a test user (ID: 'user_123') with role 'unassigned' or similar.
Ensure the current session is authenticated as a user with 'admin' privileges.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Remove the assigned role using DELETE /users/{id}/remove-role for the created user.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the dependency edge where admin creates users first, then assigns roles.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen receives real-time push notifications via Telegram bot.
strategy_items.prompt: Simulate a status change event for a report and verify that the Telegram bot receives the webhook payload correctly, triggering a push notification to the citizen.
setup_needed: Ensure a valid report exists with an active Telegram subscription for the citizen.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Verify no new reports were created; if any webhook test data was persisted, delete it to maintain system cleanliness.
strategy_items.rationale: Tests the integration between the reporting system and external Telegram notifications for real-time status updates.
